tasks.short: Advise students on curricula and career issues

steps.what: Advise students on academic and vocational curricula and career issues

tasks.design: Keep personal academic and career advice with the teacher. Existing curriculum information in {DOCS} supports the conversation without ranking students or choosing their path automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful advice depends on the student's goals, circumstances and uncertainty.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing course information supports discussion but does not replace personal advice.
tasks.still_hard: Balance interests, prerequisites and realistic career possibilities without overpromising.
tasks.human_edge: Ask clarifying questions and help the student consider trade-offs.
tasks.altitude: Advising responsibilities and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Clarify goals and refer questions outside teaching expertise.

evidence.claim: Personal advising remains a contextual conversation; access to course information does not establish an automated career recommendation.

assumptions: Boundary is personal advice, excluding formal admissions, credit recognition, registration and subsequent student choices.

The curriculum owner supplies current course and prerequisite information before s1. The student supplies goals and questions during s1; the teacher clarifies missing facts in that retained time, with no free suitability flag.
Existing student participation is unchanged outside the focal denominator. Native reference access suffices; no new tool, capture duty or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Teacher's advising remit and referral options
research_questions: Which questions need specialist educational or career counseling?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No student conversation is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions while responding to student contributions

tasks.design: Keep live discussion facilitation with the teacher, using existing prompts from {LMS}. The teacher responds to the contributions actually made and draws out different perspectives without automated participant assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Moderation depends on how a discussion develops in real time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing prompts support discussion without replacing facilitation.
tasks.still_hard: Keep the conversation accurate, inclusive and intellectually useful.
tasks.human_edge: Notice an overlooked contribution and turn disagreement into a learning opportunity.

reach.learn: Ask follow-up questions and balance participation.

evidence.claim: Live classroom moderation is human interaction rather than generation of a discussion prompt.

assumptions: Boundary is live facilitation, excluding lesson preparation, attendance recording and formal grading.
The teacher selects a topic in existing lesson preparation before s1. Students produce contributions after discussion begins within s1; no structured understanding or participation score is assumed.
Native prompt access is sufficient. No new recording, model or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
research_questions: Which moderation techniques help students explain rather than merely state an answer?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Prompt access does not remove moderation time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Specify course Web site structure and capture approved content, links and access settings
Develop or update course pages and navigation from the checked site specification
Check accessibility, content and permissions and publish the approved course site version

tasks.design: Configure course templates and controlled content imports in {LMS} or {CMS} to stage pages from the teacher's checked specification. The teacher retains content choices, accessibility and permission checks and approval before publishing each exact site version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated page creation, navigation setup and content copying can duplicate a known course structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and imports can build recurring page structures without generating educational content.
tasks.still_hard: Provide understandable navigation and ensure the correct audience can access the right material.
tasks.human_edge: Check the site from the learner's perspective and recognise misleading or inaccessible content.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive page assembly; teaching content and publication authority stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Use learner-oriented navigation and verify accessibility and access boundaries.

evidence.claim: Native course templates and imports can reduce repeated page setup when a checked content specification exists; this is an unmeasured model-knowledge proposal.

assumptions: Boundary is website development and maintenance, excluding creation of teaching materials, grading and original course scheduling.

The teacher and existing course owners provide approved content before s1. In retained s1 time the teacher captures page identifiers, titles, order, content versions, link targets, release dates, audience permissions, alternative-text requirements and changed-page scope; no free structured site manifest is assumed.
s2 builds only from the checked specification. Missing links, unsupported layouts and ambiguous permissions go to manual assembly rather than inferred settings.

s3 checks actual content, learner navigation, keyboard use, accessibility meaning and access with the appropriate test view before approving and publishing. Routine platform hosting remains unchanged.

Test native course copying and imports before custom code. Already automated page creation earns no saving. Additional focal upkeep is 8 hours per 100 baseline hours; additional platform template support is 3 other-role hours.
unknowns: Supported import format and publishing permissions
research_questions: Can native templates reduce manual page setup without introducing broken links or incorrect access?

already_counted.description: Content choices, specification capture and publication checks remain.

incremental.description: Maintain course import settings and resolve additional assembly exceptions.

approvals.approved_version: Exact staged site version, change manifest, content versions, navigation, release settings and audience permissions approved before publication in s3; any change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+25=60; gross=40, focal upkeep=8, central net=32. Conservative 5-15 allows bespoke pages and manual accessibility corrections; specification and publication checking retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in recruitment, registration and student placement

steps.what: Participate in student recruitment by explaining the programme and answering prospective students' questions
Support registration and placement activities by clarifying academic questions with responsible staff

tasks.design: Keep the teacher's recruitment and academic clarification work human, supported by current programme information in {DOCS}. Registration staff continue their existing process; no automatic student admission or placement decision is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prospective and registering students need contextual answers that a record alone does not supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing programme references can support these conversations without replacing them.
tasks.still_hard: Explain programme expectations accurately and identify questions for authorised admissions or registration staff.
tasks.human_edge: Help students understand the programme while avoiding promises beyond the teacher's remit.
tasks.altitude: Participation and academic clarification responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Clarify academic requirements and referral boundaries.

evidence.claim: The teacher's programme explanation and academic clarification are contextual participation, distinct from automated registration record processing.

assumptions: Boundary is the teacher's participation, excluding clerical registration processing, formal admissions decisions and separate ongoing career advice.

Programme owners supply current requirements before both steps. Prospective students produce recruitment questions in s1; registration staff and students provide separate registration or placement questions before or during s2. s2 does not depend on an assumed completed recruitment decision.
No structured admissibility or placement flag is presumed. Existing registration staff work remains unchanged outside the focal denominator.
Native programme access is sufficient. No new record application, data capture or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Teacher's actual recruitment and registration duties
research_questions: Which registration questions require academic clarification rather than clerical processing?

already_counted.description: Programme explanation and registration clarification remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+45=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No teacher conversation or academic clarification is removed, and clerical registration savings are outside this boundary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher retains advising, discussion and recruitment work while native course-site assembly may reduce repetitive setup.
reach: Work with instructional coordinators on accessible course navigation.
role.ambitious_version: Use any released website setup time to improve learner access and answer difficult academic questions.
